findings.containment: Jacob still comes in the ordinary bodily sense and becomes sighted; the form adds the result link without displacing that reading.

findings.title: Sight can open into recognition
findings.claim: The literal sight restoration can also carry a locally attributed recognition reading: Joseph's shirt meets his father's face before their bodies reunite.
findings.mechanism: The first-person shirt suffix makes the garment Joseph's; the cast verb and face target create contact, the face can represent the father as a whole person, and basiran's inner-cognition branch extends the restored seeing toward recognition and certainty. Before, the shirt appears only as a physical remedy; after, it also mediates an encounter and recognition before bodily reunion.
findings.reader_payoff: A reader can perceive the first reunion as passing through an object that carries the absent son's identity, while optical sight remains fully present.
findings.containment: The actual shirt-on-face contact and restored eyesight remain intact. The face-as-person facet is qualified, and the recognition line adds to rather than replaces sensory seeing.

epistemic.reason: The exact branch facets are supplied; the HFT trace is legacy_unbound, so the surviving relational application remains qualified and attributed.
